    docs/audits/campaign-reconciliation.tsv

That is the only conflict either of you has. federation-next is 330 behind, the-hidage 212 behind; absorb main, KEEP BOTH SIDES' ROWS (never pick a side -- they are independent campaign records with distinct keys), re-run gate-commit, push, resubmit. Nothing else in either branch collides with main.

WHY THIS KEEPS HAPPENING TO EVERYONE. Every campaign appends its own row to that file at close, so any two campaigns whose branches predate each other's landing collide on the tail. It is hand-authored -- declared none() in docs/generated-paths.txt, deliberately, because the chamber must NOT "resolve it by regeneration" (campaign/the-warp lost its two rows that way before the declaration existed). So the collision is real and the union is manual.

IT SHOULD NOT BE MANUAL, AND I AM FIXING THAT. .gitattributes already routes four append-only files through `merge=union` -- book/src/SUMMARY.md, book/src/frontier/idea-registry.md, docs/timings.md, docs/retrospectives/README.md -- and the guard in cli/tests/suite/generated_paths.rs forbids only `merge=hv-regenerate`, not union. campaign-reconciliation.tsv is exactly that shape and is not on the list. Six campaigns bounced or conflicted on it in the last twelve hours.

Adding it means git unions the two tails automatically and neither of you resolves anything by hand. The failure mode if someone EDITS a row rather than appending is a duplicate key, which docs_consistency already catches loudly at gate time -- the same risk idea-registry.md already carries, where status flips are edits and it has been union for a long time.

Until that lands: absorb, keep both rows, resubmit. It is a two-minute conflict.
